date-calculator.name: Date Calculator
date-calculator.tagline: Add or subtract days from a date, or find the difference between two dates.
date-calculator.metaTitle: Date Calculator - Add, Subtract & Date Difference | JaurTools
date-calculator.metaDescription: Free date calculator with two modes: add or subtract days from any date, or find the exact difference between two dates in days, weeks and months.
date-calculator.keywords: date calculator, add subtract days, date difference calculator, days between dates calculator
date-calculator.quickAnswer: This calculator has two modes. In add/subtract mode, entering 90 days after 18 October 2026 gives 16 January 2027, a Saturday. In difference mode, the gap between 18 October 2026 and 1 January 2027 is 75 days - about 10 weeks and 5 days, or 2 months and 14 days.
keyFacts: Adding or subtracting days never changes the calendar rules: month lengths and leap years apply automatically.
The difference between two dates counts whole calendar days between them, not including the end date.
Weeks are exact (7 days), but 'months' between dates is approximate because months vary in length.
Negative day entries in add/subtract mode move backwards - minus 10 days works like subtraction.
Both modes ignore time zones and work on plain calendar dates.
howTo: Choose a mode: Add / subtract days, or Difference between dates.
In Add / subtract: pick a date, enter days (use a minus sign to go backwards), and read the new date and weekday.
In Difference: pick both dates and read the gap in days, weeks and a year/month/day breakdown.
Swap the dates freely - the difference is always reported as a positive number.
Copy the result for invoices, contracts or planning documents.
date-calculator.formula:
Add/subtract: new date = start date +/- N days.
Difference: gap = |date B minus date A| in days.
Weeks = floor(days / 7), leftover = days mod 7.
Y/M/D breakdown: full years, then full months, then days - same as the Age Difference Calculator.
Example: 2026-10-18 + 90 days = 2027-01-16.
date-calculator.workedExample:
Mode: Add. Start: 18 October 2026 (Sunday). Days: 90.
1. October: 18 + 13 = 31 October (13 days used).
2. November: 30 more days -> 30 November (43 used).
3. December: 31 more days -> 31 December (74 used).
4. January: 16 more days -> 16 January 2027 (90 used).
5. Weekday: 90 = 12 weeks + 6 days, so Sunday + 6 = Saturday.
Result: 16 January 2027, Saturday.
benefits: Two essential date tools in one page - no need to open a second calculator.
Perfect for 30/60/90-day payment terms, notice periods and delivery windows.
The weekday result prevents accidental weekend scheduling.
Difference mode settles duration questions for contracts and rentals.
limitations: Business days and public holidays are not considered - this is pure calendar math.
Month and year breakdowns of a difference are calendar-based approximations.
Time zones are ignored; results are calendar dates only.
Does not validate whether a date is sensible for your purpose (for example, a past deadline).

faqs.q: What is the difference between this and Days Between Dates?
faqs.a: This tool combines two jobs: shifting a date by N days, and measuring a gap. Days Between Dates focuses on precise durations between two date-times, including hours and business days.
Yes - enter a negative number of days, or use the dedicated Subtract From a Date tool.

faqs.q: Does the difference include the end date?
faqs.a: No, it counts the days strictly between the two dates. From Monday to Tuesday is 1 day.

faqs.q: Why do months in the breakdown vary?
faqs.a: Because months are 28 to 31 days long. The breakdown counts whole calendar months first, so the same day-count can split differently depending on which months it spans.

faqs.q: Can I use it for 90-day payment terms?
faqs.a: Yes - enter 90 days from the invoice date. Just remember payment terms sometimes mean business days, which this tool does not calculate.
Yes, for any valid date. Weekday math is exact because every week is exactly 7 days.
